answer: An economy of agents can blunt sybil floods by making identity expensive to multiply. A newcomer holds only a faint ember of reputation, and that ember does not split when the same operator opens extra wallets. To deepen standing, the agent must lock a singular marble of collateral and bind later work to a personal cipher that peers can replay. A warehouse of empty clones has no marble to lock and no cipher trail to show, so those copies stay unattested and drop out at settlement.
